p: David his father: He followed David in all points that he followed the Lord.
young: When he was but sixteen years old he showed himself zealous of God's glory, and at twenty years old he abolished idolatry and restored the true religion.
the altars of Baalim in his: Which shows that he would see the reformation with his own eyes.
bones of the priests upon their: Read 2Ki 23:16.
broken down the altars and the: This great zeal of this godly king the Holy Spirit sets forth as an example and pattern to other kings and rulers, to teach them what God requires of them.
And they put it in the: Meaning Shaphan, etc.
houses which the kings of Judah: For there were many portions and pieces annexed to the temple.
faithfully: Meaning that they were in such credit for their fidelity that they made no accounts of that which they received, 2Ki 22:7,9.
book of the law of the: Read 2Ki 22:8.
the king: For the king was commanded to continually have a copy of this book and to read in it day and night, De 17:18.
rent his clothes: For sorrow that the word of God had been so long suppressed and the people kept in ignorance, considering also the curses contained in it against the transgressors.
fathers have not kept the word: Thus the godly not only lament their own sins, but also that their fathers and predecessors have offended God.
wardrobe: Meaning, either of the priests apparel or the kings.
college: Read 2Ki 22:15.
the man that sent you to: That is, to the king.
hands: This she speaks in contempt of the idolaters, who contrary to reason and nature call a god that which they have made and framed with their own hands.
tender: This declares the end of God's threatenings, to call his to repentance, and to assure the unrepentant of their destruction.
place: It may appear that very few were touched with true repentance, seeing that God spared them for a time only for the king's sake.

small: Though neither young nor old could be exempted from the curses contained in it, if they did transgress, he knew it pertained to all and was his duty to see it read to all sorts, that everyone might learn to avoid those punishments by serving God correctly.
that were present in Israel to: Because he had charge over all, and must answer for everyone that perished: he thought it his duty to see that all should make profession to receive the word of God.
